banh-can-nha-trang.name: Nha Trang rice cakes with shrimp and quail eggs
aliases: Nha Trang bánh căn with shrimp and quail eggs
banh-can-nha-trang.serving_basis: About 24 small cakes, six per person, served with greens, green mango and dipping sauce.
banh-can-nha-trang.description: Nha Trang bánh căn are small rice-flour cakes cooked individually in clay molds, with shrimp or quail eggs on top. Bếp Việt adapts a family batch using a multi-well pan and scallion-fish sauce, served with herbs and green mango to balance the savory topping.
banh-can-nha-trang.finished_dish: Small cakes with lightly golden edges and soft centers, topped with shrimp or quail egg and served hot with scallion oil, fresh herbs, green mango and fish sauce.
banh-can-nha-trang.serving: Serve the cakes as soon as they leave the mold. Add a little scallion oil, herbs and green mango, then dip lightly in fish sauce or scallion fish sauce.
tips: Resting the batter for about 30 minutes helps the rice flour hydrate; stir again before each batch because the flour settles.
Preheat the mold and brush it with only a thin film of oil. Cover briefly so the top cooks while the edges set crisp.
Do not overfill each well. Cook shrimp and quail egg through before serving.
search_terms: bánh căn with shrimp and quail egg
banh-can-nha-trang.image_alt: Small golden-edged Nha Trang bánh căn topped with shrimp and quail eggs, served with scallion oil, herbs and dipping sauce; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-can-nha-trang.time_note: About 1 hour 25 minutes, including resting the batter and cooking the cakes in batches.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Use fine rice flour; stir so it does not settle.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually until the batter is loose enough to pour.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the batter lightly.

ingredients.name: Small fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Peel, devein and pat dry.

ingredients.name: Quail eggs
ingredients.notes: Wash the shells; use one per cake or halve them for smaller molds.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Finely slice for scallion oil.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For brushing the mold and making scallion oil.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: For dipping sauce; adjust to its saltiness.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Dissolve with the fish sauce and warm water.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Add at the end for a fresh flavor.

ingredients.name: Garlic and chili
ingredients.notes: Mince; serve chili separately for children or mild eaters.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs and green mango
ingredients.notes: Wash and drain the herbs; shred the mango.

preparation_steps: Whisk rice flour with water and salt until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes, then stir again.
Peel, devein and pat the shrimp dry. Wash and drain the herbs; shred the green mango. Slice the scallions for scallion oil.
Dissolve sugar in warm water and fish sauce, then add lime, garlic and chili. Taste for a balanced sweet-sour-salty flavor.
cooking_steps: Heat a bánh căn mold or multi-well pan over medium heat. Brush each well with a very thin layer of oil.
Pour batter halfway into a well. Add one shrimp or quail egg, cover and cook for 4–6 minutes until the top sets and the topping is cooked.
Remove the cake when its edge turns golden and releases from the mold. Repeat in batches, adjusting the heat so the center cooks without darkening the base.
Warm the scallions in the remaining oil, spoon a little over the cakes and serve hot with herbs, green mango and dipping sauce.

ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-da-nang.name: Da Nang steamed scad with rice-paper rolls
aliases: Da Nang scad rolls with water spinach
Central Vietnamese steamed scad rice-paper rolls
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-da-nang.serving_basis: Four servings of steamed fish with rice paper, fresh vermicelli, greens and dipping sauce.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-da-nang.description: Steamed scad wrapped in rice paper is a simple coastal Da Nang meal. The fish is steamed with lemongrass, scallion and chili to keep its natural sweetness, then rolled with herbs, noodles and vegetables. Bếp Việt adapts a family-sized portion and includes a safe doneness check.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-da-nang.finished_dish: Tender steamed scad scented with lemongrass and scallions, wrapped in rice paper with fresh herbs, young water spinach and vermicelli; served with fish sauce or fermented anchovy dipping sauce.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-da-nang.serving: Flake the fish into pieces and check carefully for pin bones. Wrap with rice paper, noodles and greens; dip in the sweet-sour fish sauce or prepared fermented anchovy sauce.
tips: Choose fresh fish with clear eyes and firm flesh; keep the raw-fish knife and board separate from the greens.
Steam just until done so the flesh stays moist. For thicker fish, extend the cooking time and check that the flesh next to the bone is opaque.
Strain the steaming liquid and bring it to a boil before using it to thin the dipping sauce.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-da-nang.image_alt: Steamed scad with lemongrass and scallions, served with rice paper, vermicelli, fresh greens and dipping sauce; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-da-nang.time_note: About 45 minutes; steaming is quick, while most preparation time goes to the greens and dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Fresh scad
ingredients.notes: Choose 3–4 small fish and clean the gills and innards.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Bruise the stalks and place under and over the fish.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Cut into short lengths for steaming.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Leave whole or remove the seeds for a milder dish.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the steamer.

ingredients.name: Rice paper
ingredients.notes: Moisten according to the package directions before rolling.

ingredients.name: Fresh rice vermicelli
ingredients.notes: Briefly blanch if needed, then drain.

ingredients.name: Fresh greens and young water spinach
ingredients.notes: Wash well and drain; split thick water-spinach stems.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: For the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Add after the sugar dissolves.

ingredients.name: Minced garlic
ingredients.notes: Stir into the dipping sauce.

preparation_steps: Scale and clean the fish, rinse briefly and pat dry. Score shallow cuts on both sides for even cooking.
Bruise the lemongrass, slice the ginger and cut the scallions. Wash and drain the greens and young water spinach; blanch the vermicelli if needed.
Dissolve sugar in warm water and fish sauce, then add lime, garlic and chili. Taste for a gentle sweet-sour-salty balance.
cooking_steps: Line a steamer with lemongrass and arrange the fish on top. Add ginger, scallion and chili; bring the water in the steamer to a boil.
Steam for about 12–18 minutes depending on fish size. The flesh should be opaque and separate easily from the bone; if using a thermometer, the thickest part should reach at least 63°C.
Transfer the fish to a clean platter and reserve the steaming liquid. Strain it and bring it to a boil before adding a little to the dipping sauce, if desired.
Serve the hot fish with rice paper, vermicelli and greens. Flake a small portion at a time, check for bones and eat immediately.

chao-canh-quang-binh.name: Quang Binh thick-noodle soup
chao-canh-quang-binh.serving_basis: Four hot bowls of thick noodles with shrimp, fish and broth.
chao-canh-quang-binh.description: Quang Binh chao canh is not smooth rice porridge: it is a hearty soup with thick, pleasantly chewy handmade noodles and a flavorful seafood broth. Bếp Việt adapts a home pot with shrimp and fish, keeping the noodles as the defining feature and seasoning lightly to let the seafood broth shine.
chao-canh-quang-binh.finished_dish: A hot bowl of thick, tender-chewy noodles with just-cooked shrimp and fish, scallions and pepper in a clear, savory seafood broth.
chao-canh-quang-binh.serving: Divide the noodles and seafood among bowls and ladle over the hot broth. Finish with scallions, coriander and pepper; serve chili separately.
tips: If rolling the noodles at home, dust them lightly so they do not stick; shake off excess dry flour before adding them to the pot.
Cook the noodles in a gentle boil and stir the bottom of the pot at the start so they stay separate.
Add the fish near the end and maintain a moderate simmer so it cooks through without breaking apart.
chao-canh-quang-binh.image_alt: A bowl of Quang Binh chao canh with thick noodles, shrimp, fish, scallions and hot broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
chao-canh-quang-binh.time_note: About 1 hour 35 minutes including dough resting; fresh store-bought noodles shorten the preparation.

ingredients.name: All-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.notes: Sift before kneading.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Combine with the wheat flour for tender-chewy noodles.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Pour in gradually; actual absorption varies by flour.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the dough and the broth.

ingredients.name: Fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Peel and reserve heads and shells for the broth if desired.

ingredients.name: Firm-fleshed sea fish fillet
ingredients.notes: Choose fish with firm flesh and remove all bones.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the broth; some can be replaced with strained shrimp stock.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the shallots.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season after the seafood has flavored the broth.

ingredients.name: Scallions and coriander
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Ground pepper and chili
ingredients.notes: Serve on the side to adjust the heat.

preparation_steps: Combine wheat flour, rice flour and salt. Gradually add warm water and knead until smooth, elastic and no longer sticky; cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Peel the shrimp and reserve the heads and shells if using them for stock. Rinse the fish, remove all bones and cut it into bite-sized pieces.
Dust the work surface lightly, roll the dough 2–3 mm thick and cut it into moderately wide strands. Shake gently to separate them.
Mince the shallots; wash and finely slice scallions and coriander. Prepare the seasonings before cooking the noodles.
cooking_steps: Sauté the shallots in oil. If using shrimp heads, add them and stir until red, add water and simmer for 20 minutes; strain out the solids.
Bring the broth to a gentle boil and season with salt and fish sauce. Add the noodles gradually, stirring the bottom gently during the first minute so they do not stick.
When the noodles begin to float and the broth thickens slightly, add the shrimp until pink, then add the fish and cook just through.
Taste the broth and turn off the heat once the fish is done. Ladle into bowls and finish with scallions, coriander and pepper; serve chili separately.

banh-xeo-tom-nhay-quy-nhon.name: Quy Nhon sizzling pancakes with fresh shrimp
banh-xeo-tom-nhay-quy-nhon.serving_basis: About 12 small pancakes, three per person, served with greens and sweet-sour fish sauce.
banh-xeo-tom-nhay-quy-nhon.description: Quy Nhon bánh xèo tôm nhảy are usually small, crisp-edged pancakes filled with fresh local earth shrimp and eaten with greens. Bếp Việt keeps the cakes small, the batter thin and the shrimp visible, distinguishing this style from larger, richer coconut-milk versions found elsewhere.
banh-xeo-tom-nhay-quy-nhon.finished_dish: Small golden turmeric pancakes with crisp edges, earth shrimp and bean sprouts, wrapped in fresh greens and dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce.
banh-xeo-tom-nhay-quy-nhon.serving: Serve the pancakes hot with lettuce, herbs and fish sauce. Break off a bite-sized piece, wrap it in greens and dip lightly to keep the edge crisp.
tips: Spread only a thin layer of batter in a small pan; cover briefly so the shrimp cooks, then uncover to release steam and crisp the shell.
Pat the shrimp dry before adding it to the pan to prevent splatter and soggy batter.
Cook over medium heat and wait for the edges to turn golden and release before folding or removing the pancake.
search_terms: Quy Nhon bánh xèo tôm nhảy
banh-xeo-tom-nhay-quy-nhon.image_alt: Small Quy Nhon bánh xèo with crisp golden shells, earth shrimp and bean sprouts, served with fresh greens; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-xeo-tom-nhay-quy-nhon.time_note: About 55 minutes including resting the batter and cooking the pancakes in batches.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Sift to keep the batter smooth.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually until the batter coats the pan thinly.

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder
ingredients.notes: Use just enough for a light golden color.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the batter lightly.

ingredients.name: Fresh earth shrimp
ingredients.notes: Rinse, trim sharp heads and drain thoroughly; small shrimp may retain their thin shells.

ingredients.name: Bean sprouts
ingredients.notes: Wash and drain.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Finely slice and mix into the batter.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use a little for each pancake.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: For the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Dissolve in warm water.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Add at the end.

ingredients.name: Garlic and chili
ingredients.notes: Mince and adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Lettuce and fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Wash and drain thoroughly.

preparation_steps: Whisk rice flour, turmeric and salt with water until smooth. Stir in scallions, rest for 10 minutes and stir again.
Rinse the shrimp, trim sharp heads and pat thoroughly dry. Wash and drain the bean sprouts, lettuce and herbs.
Dissolve the sugar in warm water and fish sauce; once dissolved, add lime, garlic and chili. Taste before serving.
cooking_steps: Heat a small pan over medium heat and add a teaspoon of oil. Pour in a small ladle of batter and swirl to coat the base thinly.
Arrange a few shrimp and a little bean sprout over one half of the pancake. Cover for 1–2 minutes until the shrimp is cooked, then uncover to let steam escape.
Drizzle a little oil around the edge and continue cooking until the edge is crisp and releases from the pan. Fold gently or transfer the pancake whole to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining batter and filling. Serve immediately with fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce.

bun-hen-con-hen-hue.name: Hue Cồn Hến mixed clam vermicelli
bun-hen-con-hen-hue.serving_basis: Four bowls of mixed vermicelli with clams; hot clam broth is served separately for pouring as desired.
bun-hen-con-hen-hue.description: Hue bún hến is a mixed bowl of rice vermicelli with sautéed clams, fresh herbs, peanuts, rice crackers and fermented shrimp paste; hot clam broth is commonly served on the side. Bếp Việt adapts a family version with fresh clams, keeping the savory, spicy flavor while serving shrimp paste and chili separately for individual seasoning.
bun-hen-con-hen-hue.finished_dish: A bowl of vermicelli topped with fragrant clams, herbs and banana blossom, finished with peanuts, sesame and pork crackling; served with hot clam broth and chili shrimp paste on the side.
bun-hen-con-hen-hue.serving: Divide vermicelli among bowls and top with sautéed clams and greens. Sprinkle with peanuts, sesame and crackling. Serve with hot clam broth; add shrimp paste or chili to taste and mix before eating.
tips: Soak clams in clean water with a little salt to release sand, changing the water several times; discard cracked or foul-smelling shells.
Boil until shells open and discard any that remain closed; strain the cooking liquid finely to remove grit.
Wash and drain the greens and banana blossom thoroughly; mix them in just before serving to keep their crunch.
bun-hen-con-hen-hue.image_alt: Hue mixed clam vermicelli with sautéed clams, fresh herbs, banana blossom, peanuts and crackling, served with hot clam broth and chili shrimp paste; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
bun-hen-con-hen-hue.time_note: About 1 hour 20 minutes, including 30 minutes to soak the clams and release grit.

ingredients.name: Fresh clams in shell

ingredients.name: Fresh rice vermicelli

ingredients.name: Shredded banana blossom
ingredients.notes: Soak in diluted lime water, rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander and fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Wash, drain thoroughly and roughly chop.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Crush coarsely rather than grinding to powder.

ingredients.name: Toasted sesame
ingredients.notes: Toast until fragrant and cool.

ingredients.name: Pork crackling or crispy pork skin
ingredients.notes: Use a moderate amount for savory crunch.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Finely mince for sautéing the clams.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying shallots and lemongrass.

ingredients.name: Hue fermented shrimp paste
ingredients.notes: Dilute with clam broth and taste before adding.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add to the clam broth if needed.

ingredients.name: Chili and black pepper
ingredients.notes: Serve separately to adjust the heat.

preparation_steps: Soak the clams in clean water with a little salt for 30 minutes, change the water once and rinse several times to remove grit.
Shred the banana blossom and soak it in diluted lime water, then rinse. Wash and drain the herbs; crush the peanuts coarsely.
Mince the shallots, lemongrass and chili. Dilute the fermented shrimp paste with a little clam broth and strain if gritty.
Briefly blanch the vermicelli and drain. Toast the sesame if needed and prepare the crackling or crispy pork skin.
cooking_steps: Put the clams in a pot with just enough water and bring to a boil until most shells open. Turn off the heat, remove the clams and discard any that remain closed.
Strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve lined with clean cloth to remove sand. Bring the broth back to a boil, season very lightly and keep hot for serving.
Sauté shallots and lemongrass until fragrant, add the clam meat and stir-fry briefly. Add some diluted shrimp paste, taste for a savory balance and turn off the heat.
Place vermicelli in bowls and arrange clams, banana blossom and herbs on top. Sprinkle with peanuts, sesame and crackling; serve with the hot clam broth and remaining shrimp paste.
